findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "lines" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_answering_line_offer, set_up_answering_line, get_answering_line, get_line_calls, get_line_messages, get_receptionist_benchmark · Private data: get_sip_address, get_receptionist_benchmark · Public sink: set_up_answering_line, get_sip_address · Destructive: set_up_answering_line, get_receptionist_benchmark.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_answering_line_offer, set_up_answering_line, get_answering_line, get_line_calls, get_line_messages, get_receptionist_benchmark · Private data: get_sip_address, get_receptionist_benchmark · Public sink: set_up_answering_line, get_sip_address · Destructive: set_up_answering_line, get_receptionist_benchmark

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_receptionist_benchmark" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
